# P5: a real Claude connector with a `wiki` argument (for the owner)

Not tried by the agent: it needs a Claude account and a public HTTPS address. The question is whether Claude, given one connector, lists the wikis with a tool and then names the wiki in every other call.

`p5-mcp.mjs` is a throwaway MCP server with no dependencies and no sign-in. It has two tools, `list_wikis` and `read_page(wiki, path)`, and two fixed wikis (`team/wiki`, `team/wiki-b`) with a page `index` each. It serves no real data.

## Try it

1. On the test server: `node p5-mcp.mjs` (listens on port 8765; `PORT=… node p5-mcp.mjs` for another).
2. In nginx, forward one public HTTPS path to it, for example `location /p5/ { proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:8765/; }`, so the address is `https://<server>/p5/mcp`.
3. In Claude: Settings → Connectors → Add custom connector, address `https://<server>/p5/mcp`, no sign-in.
4. In a new chat with the connector on, ask: "Which wikis can I open? Read the page index from each and tell me its first line."
5. Look at `https://<server>/p5/calls` (or the server's output): the calls Claude made.
6. Remove the connector and stop the server.

## Passes when

- Claude calls `list_wikis` first, then `read_page` once per wiki with `wiki` set to `team/wiki` and `team/wiki-b`, and answers with "The first line of Wiki A." and "The first line of Wiki B.".
- Also try: "Read index" without naming a wiki. Note whether Claude asks which wiki, picks one, or calls `list_wikis`.

## If it fails

The plan's fallback: one connection per wiki, chosen when the connector is approved. Until P5 is tried, the plan treats the `wiki` argument as unconfirmed.
